correctness.rationale: For odd m each forbidden prime residue is t≡0 or 1 mod p; their disjoint local inclusion-exclusion expands to 3^{omega(m)} coprime CRT (a,b) pairs. Odd-length progression of representatives modulo ab yields the E0 parity sum over [1,m]. The mod-4 sign sequence of period four over 2m has two residual terms and yields E1; for e>=2 each admissible class mod odd m has exactly 2^{e-2} lifts t≡3 mod4. T(1)=T(2)=0. For odd primes p≠q, least positive inverses u=p^{-1} mod q and v=q^{-1} mod p satisfy pu+qv=pq+1, so u and v share parity; hence E0(pq)=-1+2(-1)^{u+1}. Prime-number-theorem equidistribution over residue classes mod fixed odd p proves sign density. Independent literal gcd enumeration agrees with the CRT formula for all n=1,...,150 (n=1 separately set to zero by definition). Finite checks corroborate the unrestricted CRT/progression argument.
